uslaw-usc-t1-s106b:
Section 106b of Title 1 of the United States Code covers amendments to the Constitution. It sits in Title 1, on general provisions, in the chapter on acts, resolutions, and the formal steps of enactment. The section states what is to happen when an amendment has been adopted. The trigger is formal notice at the National Archives that an amendment put to the states has been adopted under the terms of the Constitution.

On such notice, the Archivist of the United States must at once have the amendment published. His certificate is to go with the text of the amendment. The certificate states the states that adopted it and that it has become valid for all ends and purposes. The text is current through Public Law 119-134.
uslaw-usc-t2-s276b: Section 276b of Title 2 of the United States Code covers travel expenses of the Legislative Counsel of the Senate. It sits in Chapter 9 of that title, on the Office of Legislative Counsel. The rule ties such spending to the rules that bind Senate travel in general. Funds spent by that office for travel are subject to the same rules and limits as Senate travel paid from the contingent fund. Those rules are set by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration.
